notes: The study identifies spatially and temporally linked paired metamorphism in the Western Dharwar Craton (WDC), South India, dating to the Archaean-Proterozoic boundary (c. 2.53–2.41 Ga).
Paired metamorphism is defined as the occurrence of contrasting thermal gradients in orogen-parallel metamorphic belts of the same age.
In the context of the Early Earth, paired metamorphism is recognized by the duality of intermediate T/P (cooler) and high T/P (warmer) thermal regimes.
The research compares a medium-grade (MG) domain, characterized by pelitic schists, with a high-grade (HG) domain containing mafic and metasedimentary granulites.
The MG domain recorded cooler, intermediate T/P metamorphism in the kyanite stability field with maximum temperatures of approximately 630–650°C.
MG rocks followed clockwise P-T paths and 'pulsating orogenesis,' featuring multiple short-lived burial-exhumation and heating-cooling cycles.
Thermal history in the MG domain was relatively short-lived, with crustal residence of 10–20 Myrs and fast cooling rates of 10–20°C/Myr.
The HG domain recorded warmer, high T/P metamorphism in the sillimanite stability field with peak temperatures between 800–870°C.
HG rocks followed a monocyclic clockwise P-T path representing a single prograde heating event with recurring burial-exhumation stages.
The HG domain experienced extremely long-lived crustal residence (~238 Myrs) and ultra-slow cooling (~2°C/Myr) and exhumation (~0.1 mm/yr) rates.
Thermobaric (T/P) ratios at the metamorphic peak are used as primary indicators to monitor tectonic settings and distinguish between different orogenic processes.
The study suggests a shift from 'stagnant lid' plume-driven vertical tectonics to asymmetric plate subduction at the Archaean-Proterozoic boundary.
The 'peel-back convergence' model is proposed to explain the spatial pairing of the Thickened Crustal Zone (TCZ) and the Peel-off Zone (PoZ).
In the peel-back model, the TCZ typically yields intermediate T/P metamorphism while the PoZ yields high T/P metamorphism.
Pulsating orogenesis is defined as an orogeny consisting of several short-lived heating-cooling and burial-exhumation stages as part of multiple metamorphic cycles.
Advanced techniques such as garnet-biotite diffusion chronometry and monazite chemical dating were used to reconstruct the P-T-t paths of the investigated rocks.

flashcards.q: What two domains in the Western Dharwar Craton (WDC) were compared to demonstrate paired metamorphism?
flashcards.a: The study compared the medium-grade (MG) domain, containing rocks like pelitic schist, and the high-grade (HG) domain, containing mafic and metasedimentary granulites.

flashcards.q: How do the thermobaric (T/P) ratios differ between the MG and HG domains of the WDC?
flashcards.a: The MG domain records cooler, intermediate T/P metamorphism, while the HG domain records warmer, high T/P metamorphism (800–870 °C/GPa).

flashcards.q: Which mineral stability fields characterize the peak temperatures of the MG and HG domains?
flashcards.a: The MG domain reached peak temperatures in the kyanite stability field (~630-650 °C), whereas the HG domain reached peak temperatures in the sillimanite field (~800–870 °C).

flashcards.q: What is the difference in crustal residence time between the MG and HG domains?
flashcards.a: The MG domain had a short-lived residence of approximately 10-20 Myrs, while the HG domain had an extremely long-lived residence of approximately 238 Myrs.

flashcards.q: Compare the metamorphic cooling rates of the MG and HG domains.
flashcards.a: The MG domain experienced fast cooling at 10-20 °C/Myr, whereas the HG domain underwent ultra-slow cooling at approximately 2 °C/Myr.

flashcards.q: How do the exhumation rates of the two domains in the WDC compare?
flashcards.a: The MG domain had faster exhumation rates of 0.6-2.0 mm/yr, while the HG domain had a much slower rate of approximately 0.1 mm/yr.

flashcards.q: During what geological timeframe did the coeval metamorphism in the WDC occur?
flashcards.a: Metamorphism in both domains occurred as part of the same orogenesis between approximately 2.53 and 2.41 Ga, at the Archaean-Proterozoic boundary.

flashcards.q: What tectonic model is proposed to explain the paired metamorphism in the WDC?
flashcards.a: The study suggests the development of a 'peel-back convergence' style of plate tectonics.

flashcards.q: How is 'pulsating orogenesis' defined in this study?
flashcards.a: It refers to orogenesis consisting of several short-lived heating-cooling and burial-exhumation stages as part of multiple metamorphic cycles, each with a characteristic P-T path.

flashcards.q: What are the two spatially adjacent tectonic domains identified in thermo-mechanical models of peel-back convergence?
flashcards.a: The two domains are the Thickened Crustal Zone (TCZ), associated with intermediate T/P, and the Peel-off Zone (PoZ), associated with high T/P.

flashcards.q: According to Miyashiro, what is the defining feature of paired metamorphism?
flashcards.a: It is the presence of contrasting thermal gradients (high P/T vs. low P/T) in orogen-parallel metamorphic belts of the same age.

flashcards.q: What metamorphic indicators are used to identify fossil convergent plate margins in ancient orogenic belts?
flashcards.a: Deep burials during high-pressure (HP) metamorphism, steeper dP/dT gradients, and clockwise (CW) P-T paths of evolution.

flashcards.q: Why is the classic definition of paired metamorphism (low T/P vs. high P/T) modified for the Archaean Earth?
flashcards.a: The Archaean Earth was hotter, which inhibited the formation of cold lawsonite-blueschists or eclogites, requiring a shift to comparing intermediate T/P and high T/P gradients.

flashcards.q: Which analytical techniques were used to determine the temporal history of the WDC rocks?
flashcards.a: The study used garnet-biotite diffusion chronometry and monazite chemical dating techniques.

mcqs.question: The study suggests that the Western Dharwar Craton (WDC) provides evidence for a specific tectonic transition at the Archean-Proterozoic boundary. Which transition is it?
options: A) From asymmetric subduction to vertical plume-driven tectonics
B) From a hot stagnant lid regime to a peel-back convergence mode
C) From oceanic subduction to a permanent stagnant lid regime
D) From high-pressure eclogite formation to low-pressure granulite facies

mcqs.question: In the context of the Western Dharwar Craton, which mineral stability field is characteristic of the peak metamorphic conditions in the Medium-Grade (MG) domain?
options: A) Sillimanite
B) Glaucophane
C) Kyanite
D) Jadeite

mcqs.question: Based on the geochronological dataset mentioned, the metamorphism in both the MG and HG domains is considered coeval and occurred during which time period?
Which of the following best describes the contrast in exhumation and cooling rates between the Medium-Grade (MG) and High-Grade (HG) domains?
options: A) The MG domain experienced ultra-slow cooling (2 °C/Myr) and slow exhumation (0.1 mm/yr).
B) The HG domain experienced fast cooling (10-20 °C/Myr) and fast exhumation (0.6-2 mm/yr).
C) The MG domain showed faster cooling and exhumation compared to the ultra-slow history of the HG domain.
D) Both domains shared identical cooling and exhumation rates despite different peak temperatures.

mcqs.question: The term 'pulsating orogenesis' is used in the study to describe the MG domain's history. What does this term specifically imply?
options: A) A single, long-lived heating event that lasted over 200 million years.
B) Several short-lived cycles of burial-exhumation and heating-cooling.
C) A tectonic regime driven exclusively by periodic mantle plume arrivals.
D) The rhythmic formation of high-pressure blueschists in a cold subduction zone.

mcqs.question: Why does the concept of 'paired metamorphism' in the Archean differ from the classical Phanerozoic model involving blueschists and eclogites?
options: A) Archean subduction was too fast for mineral equilibrium to be reached.
B) The lack of oxygen in the Archean atmosphere changed the chemistry of metamorphic fluids.
C) The hotter Archean mantle inhibited the formation of cold lawsonite-blueschists.
D) Archean crust was too thick to allow for the deep burial required for high-pressure rocks.

mcqs.question: According to the study's P-T-t path reconstructions, what is a primary difference in the metamorphic 'path' of the HG domain versus the MG domain?
options: A) The HG domain followed a monocyclic prograde heating event, while the MG domain recorded multiple cycles.
B) The MG domain followed a counter-clockwise path, while the HG domain was strictly clockwise.
C) The HG domain stayed in the kyanite stability field, while the MG domain reached sillimanite stability.
D) The HG domain showed rapid burial and exhumation, whereas the MG domain was long-lived at depth.

mcqs.question: In the 'peel-back convergence' thermo-mechanical model, how are the TCZ (Thickened Crustal Zone) and PoZ (Peel-off Zone) domains distinguished by their thermobaric (T/P) ratios?
options: A) Both domains show high T/P ratios, but differ in their maximum pressure (PMax).
B) The TCZ shows intermediate T/P ratios, while the PoZ shows high T/P ratios.
C) The TCZ shows high T/P ratios, while the PoZ shows intermediate T/P ratios.
D) Both domains show intermediate T/P ratios, but differ in their maximum temperature (TMax).

mcqs.question: What evidence from the Western Dharwar Craton study suggests that the MG and HG domains represent a spatially and temporally linked pair rather than unrelated terranes?
options: A) They show identical P-T paths of evolution and the same peak thermal gradients.
B) They both record uniform burial to lower crustal depths and were coeval during the same orogenesis.
C) They both contain the same proportions of mafic and metasedimentary granulites.
D) They both record ultra-slow cooling rates of 2 °C/Myr over a period of 238 Myrs.

mcqs.question: How does the documented 'residence time' in the lower-mid-crust provide a critical clue to the tectonic environment of the HG domain?
options: A) The short 10-20 Myr residence suggests it was part of a stable, cold subduction interface.
B) The extremely long 238 Myr residence suggests it remained at depth within a peel-off zone (PoZ).
C) The 238 Myr residence time proves that plate tectonics was not active during that period.
D) The residence time is irrelevant; only the peak pressure (PMax) identifies the tectonic setting.
